text:
Registered residential sales reached 14,433 units in the last four weeks, totaling AED 42,636,636,091. This volume represents a 41.6 percent increase compared to the previous four-week period. Mortgage registrations were recorded separately at 5,985. The off-plan share of sales stood at 57.7 percent, slightly lower than the 59.4 percent observed in the prior period.

The median residential price per square foot rose to AED 1,689, marking a 1.4 percent increase from the previous benchmark of AED 1,665. Top performing areas by sales volume include Dubai South with 3,100 units and Jumeirah Village Circle with 2,513 units over the last twelve weeks. Dubai Creek Harbour showed the strongest price momentum among major communities, with a 7.5 percent rise in median price per square foot.

Rental activity remained robust with 110,329 contracts registered. Renewals accounted for 51.6 percent of these transactions. The median annual residential rent was AED 68,729. In terms of yield, Zaabeel First led with an estimated gross yield of 8.8 percent for flats, followed by International City Phase 1 at 8.6 percent. Town Square, Dubai Sports City, and Dubai Production City also recorded yields above 6.5 percent.

Market watchers should note significant price divergence in specific communities. Al Yufrah 1 saw a 41.5 percent increase in median price per square foot, while Jumeirah Lakes Towers cooled by 18.8 percent. An anomaly monitor flagged 979 sales in the last 60 days that deviated more than 35 percent from comparable medians. These figures are derived from registered DLD data and Ejari contracts, using medians and benchmark filters that exclude bulk deals, partial shares, and statistical outliers.

facts.ranking_rule: communities with at least 30 eligible sales in both 12-week windows; yields also need 30 rent contracts of the same property type
